subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What are the main kinds of issues these support tickets are about?

judge.implied_focus: The nature/taxonomy of support ticket issues -- characterizing what each ticket is about across categorization, affected surface, impact, and cause

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query with a top-level taxonomy of issue kinds -- the core facet of the focus.

per_column.name: issue_subcategory
per_column.rationale: Refines the categorization at finer granularity, a coherent second level of the same taxonomy.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Orthogonal facet locating the issue in the product surface, enriching characterization of what tickets are about.

per_column.name: impact_scope
per_column.rationale: Characterizes breadth of impact, a meaningful facet of issue nature beyond bare type.

per_column.name: business_impact_signal
per_column.rationale: Adds a business-consequence facet, coherently attached to the issue-characterization focus.

per_column.name: root_cause_class
per_column.rationale: Explains why issues occur, a strong analytical predictor/attribute complementing the what.

judge.rationale: All six columns converge tightly on a single, data-inferable focus: characterizing the nature of support-ticket issues. They form a well-differentiated multi-facet structure -- a two-level type taxonomy (category/subcategory), an affected-surface facet, two impact facets (scope and business impact), and a causal facet (root cause) -- rather than a restatement or generic noise. The granularity is useful and the values are semantically rich and non-trivial. An analyst could directly act on this: prioritize by category/impact, target components, and address root causes. Minor deduction to structure because business_impact_signal and impact_scope partially overlap conceptually, but overall this strongly realises the focus-inference claim.
